description: Whole-face proportional dimensions: face shape, facial-thirds balance, cheekbone prominence, malar projection, midface morphology, forehead. Captures the macro-level face morphology that's not localized to any single feature. Dimensions draw from craniofacial anthropometry (Farkas), facial-aesthetics literature (Powell-Humphreys, Ricketts), and contemporary aesthetic-medicine references on the diverse-patient-population face.

dimensions.scale_citation: Aligned with cosmetology-and-anthropometry shape descriptors used in styling and forensic-anthropology literature.
dimensions.description: Macro-level shape of the face derived from facial outline (forehead width, cheekbone width, jaw width, face length).

values.definition: Length approximately 1.5x width; balanced forehead and jaw with widest point at cheekbones.
Length and width approximately equal; soft jaw and forehead curves.
Length and width approximately equal; angular jaw and forehead.
Wide forehead, narrow jaw, often with a pointed chin.
Narrow forehead and jaw with widest point at cheekbones; pronounced cheek prominence.
Length substantially greater than width; balanced forehead and jaw.
Wide jaw, narrow forehead — opposite of heart-shape.
Notable left-right facial asymmetry as the dominant feature.

dimensions.scale_citation: Farkas LG (1994). Anthropometry of the Head and Face, 2nd Edition. Aesthetic reference: upper third (trichion-glabella), middle third (glabella-subnasale), lower third (subnasale-menton) approximately equal in the European-population norm.
dimensions.description: Relative proportions of the three classical facial thirds.

values.definition: All three vertical thirds approximately equal.
Forehead substantially longer than the other thirds.
Midface (glabella to subnasale) substantially longer.
Lower face (subnasale to menton) substantially longer; common with prognathism or chin elongation.
Low hairline; reduced forehead height.
Reduced lower-face vertical dimension; common with retrognathia.

observability.notes: Hairline position can be obscured by hairstyle; trichion may not be reliably visible.

dimensions.scale_citation: Aligned with the malar-augmentation literature; Ricketts esthetic plane references the malar region.
dimensions.description: Anterior projection of the zygomatic prominence.

values.definition: Cheekbones not visible as a discrete landmark.
Cheekbones visible but not prominent.
Pronounced anterior projection; defined cheekbone landmarks. Common in some East Asian, indigenous American, and Slavic populations.

dimensions.scale_citation: Farkas LG (1994). Reference: bizygomatic breadth (zy-zy) is typically the widest face dimension in the European-population norm.
dimensions.description: Width of the face at the cheekbones, proportional to face height.

values.definition: Bizygomatic breadth narrow relative to face height.
Bizygomatic breadth in proportional reference range.
Bizygomatic breadth substantially wide; common in East Asian and indigenous populations.

dimensions.scale_citation: Aligned with facial-aging and aesthetic-medicine descriptors of the midface region.
dimensions.description: Soft-tissue contour of the midface (the region between the lower eyelid and the upper lip).

values.definition: Anterior midface fullness; smooth nasolabial fold; defined cheek apple.
Average midface fullness.
Reduced midface fullness; deepened nasolabial fold; visible tear-trough; mid-cheek descent.
Pronounced anterior midface fullness — constitutional or augmented.

dimensions.scale_citation: Farkas LG (1994). Anthropometry of the Head and Face. Reference: forehead height (trichion to glabella) approximately equal to the other facial thirds in the aesthetic norm.
dimensions.description: Vertical dimension of the forehead from hairline (trichion) to glabella, proportional to lower facial thirds.

values.definition: Forehead height substantially below proportional reference; low hairline.
Forehead height approximately matches other facial thirds.
Forehead height substantially above proportional reference; high hairline or recession.

observability.notes: Hairstyle and grooming substantially affect visible forehead height; observation should reflect visible state.

dimensions.scale_citation: Aligned with aesthetic-medicine descriptors of forehead morphology used in fillers / forehead-augmentation context.
dimensions.description: Profile shape of the forehead in lateral view.

values.definition: Smoothly rounded forehead profile; soft slope.
Forehead nearly vertical in profile; minimal anterior curvature.
Forehead slopes posteriorly from glabella; common in male morphology with prominent supraorbital ridges.
Pronounced anterior projection of the frontal bone; less common variant.

references: Farkas LG (1994). Anthropometry of the Head and Face, 2nd Edition. Raven Press.
Powell N, Humphreys B (1984). Proportions of the Aesthetic Face. Thieme.
Ricketts RM (1982). Divine proportion in facial esthetics. Clinics in Plastic Surgery, 9(4): 401-422.

Sundaram H, Liew S, Signorini M, et al. (2016). Global aesthetics consensus: hyaluronic acid fillers and botulinum toxin type A — recommendations for combined treatment and optimizing outcomes in diverse patient populations. Plastic and Reconstructive Surgery, 137(5).
